gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.
Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
gaps.hint: tell sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.
